Task Guide:

Simulate the fracture behavior of a Σ3(111) symmetric tilt grain boundary (STGB) in body-centered cubic (BCC) iron using LAMMPS. The simulation should begin by reading a pre-generated grain boundary structure file (present at /structures/task_9/Fe_110_sig3.txt) that defines a bicrystal with a tilt direction of <110> and a grain boundary plane of <111>. The simulation should use metal units and atome_style atomic, and box should have periodic boundary conditions in all directions. After initialization, perform an energy minimization using the conjugate gradient (CG) algorithm with force and energy tolerances of 1.0e-15 and a maximum of 1000 iterations and use the EAM potential present at (/potentials/EAM/Fe-C_Hepburn_Ackland.eam.fs). The box should be allowed to relax along the x and z directions while maintaining a fixed y-direction. Following minimization, apply uniaxial tensile loading perpendicular to the grain boundary (y-direction). Atoms far from the boundary should be deleted to avoid artifacts, and atoms at the edges should be fixed before the deformation begins. The strain should be applied in increments, with the fixed groups being displaced incrementally, followed by energy minimization at each step. During the simulation, compute the stress tensor components and store stress-strain data in a text file called stress_strain.txt. The file should contain strain values and stress components converted from bars to GPa in the format strain,stress_xx,stress_yy,stress_zz without any column names or metadata. As the final result, report the maximum tensile stress (in GPa) along the x-direction achieved prior to the onset of plastic deformation or structural instability, identified as the first significant drop in the stress-strain response. Make sure all the associated files for this task (input files, log files, any other files) are in the /results/md_tutorials/13_July_2025/tool_calling/claude_35/comprehensive/task_9/task_9_trial_4 directory. You can use the available I/O tools (e.g., write_file) make new files .etc. Whatever potentials you need to run the simulation, you can find them at /potentials/. A type of potential can be accessed by /potentials/TYPE where TYPE can be [EAM, TERSOFF, REAXFF] which further contains the exact potential files. Note that in case of reaxff potentials, pair style 'reax/c' has been renamed to 'reaxff' and always use NULL for the control file (cfile), for example, this syntax is correct : pair_style reaxff NULL. If the task is to give the final output as a scalar, only return the numerical value, without any units.

{"path": "/results/md_tutorials/13_July_2025/tool_calling/claude_35/comprehensive/task_9/task_9_trial_4/gb_tensile.in", "content": "# LAMMPS input script for Fe grain boundary tensile test
units metal
atom_style atomic
boundary p p p

# Read structure
read_data /structures/task_9/Fe_110_sig3.txt

# Define potential
pair_style eam/fs
pair_coeff * * /potentials/EAM/Fe-C_Hepburn_Ackland.eam.fs Fe

# Energy minimization
fix 1 all box/relax x 0.0 z 0.0
minimize 1.0e-15 1.0e-15 1000 1000
unfix 1

# Define groups for fixed regions and delete far atoms
group edge_atoms delete
group fixed_bottom delete
group fixed_top delete

# Setup for tensile deformation
variable strain equal 0.0
variable strain_rate equal 0.001
variable N_steps equal 1000
variable cur_step equal 0

# Output settings
variable stress_xx equal pxx*1.0e-4  # Convert from bars to GPa
variable stress_yy equal pyy*1.0e-4
variable stress_zz equal pzz*1.0e-4
variable tmp equal v_strain
fix data all print 1 "${tmp} ${stress_xx} ${stress_yy} ${stress_zz}" file stress_strain.txt screen no

# Main deformation loop
label loop_strain
  variable disp equal ly*${strain_rate}
  displace_atoms fixed_top move 0 ${disp} 0
  displace_atoms fixed_bottom move 0 -${disp} 0
  minimize 1.0e-15 1.0e-15 1000 1000
  variable strain equal ${strain}+${strain_rate}
  variable cur_step equal ${cur_step}+1
  if "${cur_step} < ${N_steps}" then "jump SELF loop_strain""}
